record.paper_title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in bounded convex domains in ℂ^N
record.original_question: Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^N be a bounded convex domain whose boundary contains no non-trivial analytic discs. Must it be true that there is no example in which Ω is essentially visible but not visible? Equivalently, does there exist such a bounded convex domain that is essentially visible, in the sense that for every pair of distinct boundary points p and q there is a compact set K ⊂⊂ Ω met by some geodesic segment joining any sequences z_k → p and w_k → q, but not visible in the stronger sense that every such sequence of geodesic segments must eventually meet a fixed compact set? The paper also asks the same existence question under the additional assumption that Ω is smoothly bounded.

evidence.quote: Question 3.3. Does there exist a bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ C^N with no non-trivial analytic discs in the boundary which is essentially visible but not visible? Does there exist a smoothly bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ C^N which is essentially visible but not visible?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ be a bounded convex domain, and let $k_\Omega$ denote its Kobayashi distance. A geodesic segment in $\Omega$ is an isometric embedding $\sigma:[a,b]\to(\Omega,k_\Omega)$.

Say that $\Omega$ is visible if for every pair of distinct boundary points $p,q\in\partial\Omega$ there exist neighborhoods $U_p,U_q$ of $p,q$ in $\overline{\Omega}$ with $\overline{U_p}\cap\overline{U_q}=\emptyset$ and a compact set $K\subset\Omega$ such that every $(1,\kappa)$-quasi-geodesic segment (for some fixed $\kappa\ge 0$, equivalently every geodesic segment) joining a point of $U_p\cap\Omega$ to a point of $U_q\cap\Omega$ intersects $K$.

Say that $\Omega$ is essentially visible if for every pair of distinct boundary points $p,q\in\partial\Omega$ and every pair of sequences $z_k\to p$, $w_k\to q$ in $\Omega$, there exists a compact set $K\subset\Omega$ (possibly depending on the sequences) and, for each $k$, a geodesic segment $\sigma_k$ joining $z_k$ and $w_k$ such that $\sigma_k\cap K\neq\emptyset$ for infinitely many $k$.

Assume further that $\partial\Omega$ contains no non-trivial analytic discs, i.e., no non-constant holomorphic map $\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}^N$ has image contained in $\partial\Omega$.

(a) Does there exist such a bounded convex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^N$ that is essentially visible but not visible?

(b) Does there exist a smoothly bounded convex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^N$ that is essentially visible but not visible?
